title: backend-skeleton native export envelope (draft, shadow only)
description: Shape of the object that createNativeExportEnvelope in native-export-envelope.mjs returns and verifyNativeExportEnvelope accepts (schema sbf.game-native-export-envelope/draft-1, envelope_revision 2). The envelope binds the exact bytes of one engine export and of the source files it came from; it interprets nothing and verifies nothing about the engine. Every claim is false by construction. This file checks shape only: it cannot see bytes, so a byte hash that does not belong to the payload still validates, and it cannot express that source input paths are unique. The test native-export-envelope-schema.test.mjs lists where this schema is stricter or looser than the code.

envelope_revision.description: Revision of the envelope shape inside the draft.

status.description: bound-uninterpreted: the bytes are bound to this envelope and nothing in them was interpreted. It is not a support, runtime or correctness status.

engine.description: The engine the producer says the export belongs to. There is no value for an unknown engine: an engine outside this list is rejected, not recorded as unknown.

evidence_class.description: How the producer says the export was made. Which classes an engine accepts is stated by the allOf rules below.

engine_version.description: Free text from the producer, not verified.

platform.description: Free text from the producer, not verified.

source_inputs.description: Exact source files the export was made from, sorted by path by the builder. Required to be non-empty for the evidence class source-export. Paths are unique in the code; this schema cannot express that.

size_bytes.description: Byte length, a non-negative safe integer.

media_type.description: type/subtype without white space, the rule of the code. The pattern is the whole check and nothing parses the text, so a parameter written without white space is accepted as part of the subtype (text/plain;charset=utf-8 is accepted) and white space anywhere is rejected (text/plain; charset=utf-8 is rejected), as is a missing slash.

portable_path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path: non-empty, no leading slash, no drive prefix, no backslash, no NUL, and no empty, dot or dot-dot segment.

producer.description: Declaration of the tool that made the export. Nothing verifies it: implementation_sha256 only has to look like a digest, and claims.producer_identity_verified stays false.

export_artifact.description: Identity of the exported payload: the SHA-256 and the length of its exact bytes. Formatting-only changes of the JSON give another identity.

source_artifact.description: Identity of one source file: the SHA-256 and the length of its exact bytes.

source_input.description: One exact source file bound to the export.

payload_descriptor.description: Not authoritative. A convenience copy of what the payload says about itself: declared_schema is the value of the payload's own string property schema (null when it has none) and top_level_keys are its top-level property names, sorted. Neither is verified against anything and neither is an identity or a trust signal; the bytes in artifact are the only binding.

claims.description: Every claim is false by construction. The envelope never asserts that the producer was identified, that the engine was run, or that edges or state transitions were established.
